  verify:
    # The weekly run is build-chain's alone.
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm

      # Both re:cinq libraries install from the npm registry, whose tarballs ship
      # built code, so no dependency needs a lifecycle script.
      - name: Install
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      # The api tests run against a real mongod, ~100MB that would otherwise be
      # downloaded again on every run. Keyed on the pinned version.
      - name: Cache the mongod the api tests start
        uses: actions/cache@0057852bfaa89a56745cba8c7296529d2fc39830 # v4
        with:
          path: ~/.cache/mongodb-binaries
          key: mongod-${{ runner.os }}-${{ hashFiles('apps/api/test/mongoTestServer.ts') }}

      # A git or file dependency skips the registry the published libraries exist to prove (#13).
      - name: Keep dependency specifiers on the npm registry
        run: npm run check:dependencies

      # The engine's package root pulls every provider SDK into the browser, and booking data must never touch storage.
      # A test file ships in no bundle, so it may import the engine's recordedFrames; shipped code never does.
      - name: Keep HAL Engine and browser storage out of the web app
        run: |
          if grep -rnE "from ['\"]@re-cinq/hal-engine|import\(['\"]@re-cinq/hal-engine" apps/web/src --exclude='*.test.ts' --exclude='*.test.tsx'; then
            echo "shipped apps/web code must not import @re-cinq/hal-engine" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if jq -e '.dependencies["@re-cinq/hal-engine"]' apps/web/package.json > /dev/null; then
            echo "apps/web may list @re-cinq/hal-engine under devDependencies only" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if grep -rnE "localStorage|sessionStorage|indexedDB|fetch\(|sendBeacon" apps/web/src/chat apps/web/src/screens apps/web/src/personas; then
            echo "apps/web chat code must not touch browser storage or send anything but the socket" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      # The model allowlist gates what configuration/ reads; a second reader would bypass it.
      - name: Read model, region and provider settings only in the api configuration
        run: |
          if grep -rnE "process\.env" apps packages --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=dist \
            | grep -E "MODEL|REGION|LOCATION|PROVIDER" | grep -v '^apps/api/src/configuration/'; then
            echo "only apps/api/src/configuration/ may read a model, region or provider value from process.env" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      # Declared twice, the band and the model's rule drift apart silently.
      - name: Keep the AI disclosure text in @support-agent/disclosure
        run: |
          if grep -rn "AI-assistent\|kunstig intelligens" apps/api/src apps/web/src; then
            echo "apps must import the AI disclosure from @support-agent/disclosure" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      # example.com until KU-30 names the domain people who may read a conversation work at.
      - name: Keep human IAM bindings inside infra/terraform/access
        run: node --experimental-strip-types scripts/check-deploy-invariants.ts infra/terraform --domain example.com

      # SC-002: the transport seam only holds if fetchTransport is the one way out; a second caller would skip deadline, retry and redaction.
      - name: Keep network access in the TMS client's transport.ts
        run: |
          if grep -rnE "\bfetch\(|['\"](node:)?(http|https|undici)['\"]" packages/tms-client/src --include='*.ts' | grep -v '^packages/tms-client/src/transport\.ts:'; then
            echo "only packages/tms-client/src/transport.ts may reference fetch, undici, http or https" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      # The reader prints whole conversations to an operator's terminal: never into a log, onto the network, or into the running service.
      # httpConversationHandler.ts is the deliberate HTTP-adapter exception to the import ban (SC-005/RD-13).
      - name: Keep the conversation reader offline and out of the running service
        run: |
          if grep -rnE "from ['\"](node:)?(http|https|ws|express)['\"]|from ['\"][^'\"]*shared/logger" apps/api/src/reader --exclude="httpConversationHandler.ts"; then
            echo "apps/api/src/reader must not import the application logger, express, http, https or ws (httpConversationHandler.ts is exempt)" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if grep -rnE "from ['\"][^'\"]*/reader/" apps/api/src/tools apps/api/src/escalation apps/api/src/start-server.ts; then
            echo "the running service must not reach apps/api/src/reader" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if grep -nE "from ['\"](mongodb|[^'\"]*readConversation)" apps/api/src/reader/conversationView.ts; then
            echo "conversationView.ts must stay pure: no mongodb, no readConversation" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          if grep -nE "from ['\"]mongodb" apps/api/src/reader/httpConversationHandler.ts; then
            echo "httpConversationHandler.ts must not import mongodb" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      # SC-004: a second timer would be one that shutdown does not clear.
      - name: Keep exactly one setInterval in the api, in shared/periodicJobs.ts
        run: |
          count=$(grep -rn "setInterval(" apps/api/src | wc -l)
          if [ "$count" -ne 1 ]; then
            echo "apps/api/src must hold exactly one setInterval call, found $count; add a job to startPeriodicJobs instead" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      # Only a reader may reach a vendor; the diff, the CLI and the freshness check run on recorded values.
      - name: Keep vendor SDKs inside the drift readers
        run: |
          if grep -rnE "(from|import\() *['\"](@google-cloud/|@google/genai|@anthropic-ai/|openai|@aws-sdk/|@re-cinq/hal-engine)" \
            packages/control-drift scripts --include='*.ts' --exclude-dir=node_modules --exclude-dir=dist \
            | grep -v '^packages/control-drift/src/readers/'; then
            echo "only packages/control-drift/src/readers/ may import a vendor SDK" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Lint
        run: npm run lint

      - name: Typecheck
        run: npm run typecheck

      - name: Test
        run: npm test

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      # CR-005: every pull request, whether or not anyone ran the recorder.
      - name: Scan committed TMS fixtures for personal data and credentials
        run: |
          node packages/tms-client/scripts/scan-fixtures.mjs
          node packages/tms-client/scripts/scan-fixtures.mjs apps/api/stand-in-tms

      # Lore's lore_list_tests reads this output; an entry printing anything but {id, name, file} objects breaks it silently.
      - name: Check every Lore test-command list prints a JSON array of tests
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          file=.lore/test-commands.yml
          cwds=$(sed -n 's/^  cwd: //p' "$file")
          lists=$(sed -n 's/^  list: //p' "$file")
          if [ "$(echo "$cwds" | wc -l)" -ne "$(echo "$lists" | wc -l)" ]; then
            echo "$file: every entry needs exactly one cwd and one list" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          paste -d '\t' <(echo "$cwds") <(echo "$lists") | while IFS=$'\t' read -r cwd list; do
            echo "::group::$cwd: $list"
            (cd "$cwd" && bash -c "$list") > "$RUNNER_TEMP/lore-list.json"
            if ! jq -e 'type == "array" and length > 0 and all(.[]; (.id | type) == "string" and (.name | type) == "string" and (.file | type) == "string")' "$RUNNER_TEMP/lore-list.json" > /dev/null; then
              echo "$cwd: '$list' did not print a non-empty JSON array of {id, name, file}" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
            echo "$(jq length "$RUNNER_TEMP/lore-list.json") tests listed"
            echo "::endgroup::"
          done

      # The chat screen shows persona labels only; a persona's prompt prose or routing keywords in the bundle would publish the agent's instructions.
      - name: Keep persona prompt text out of the web bundle
        run: |
          node --input-type=module -e "
            const {PERSONA_REGISTRY} = await import('./apps/api/dist/prompt/personas.js');
            const prompts = Object.values(PERSONA_REGISTRY.personas).flatMap((persona) => [persona.overlay, ...persona.match]);
            console.log(['PERSONA_VOICE_PLACEHOLDER', ...prompts].filter(Boolean).join('\\n'));
          " > "$RUNNER_TEMP/persona-prompt-text.txt"
          if grep -rnF -f "$RUNNER_TEMP/persona-prompt-text.txt" apps/web/dist; then
            echo "apps/web/dist must not contain a persona overlay, match keyword or PERSONA_VOICE_PLACEHOLDER" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      # A tool registered without its Danish sentences must fail here, not render a gap.
      - name: Re-record the registered tool names and fail on drift
        run: |
          npm run record-tool-names -w @support-agent/api
          git diff --exit-code apps/web/src/chat/__fixtures__/tool-names.json

  browser:
    # The weekly run is build-chain's alone.
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      - name: Install Chromium
        run: npx playwright install --with-deps chromium
        working-directory: apps/web

      - name: Browser tests
        run: npm run test:browser

  # A stopped schedule looks like "nothing drifted"; only the age of the newest reading tells them apart.
  # A missing compliance-readings branch fails the second checkout: nothing has ever been read.
  reading-freshness:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          ref: compliance-readings
          path: compliance-readings
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'

      - name: Check the newest retention reading is under two schedule intervals old
        run: node scripts/check-reading-freshness.ts compliance-readings/observations/retention.jsonl

  chart:
    # The weekly run is build-chain's alone.
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: azure/setup-helm@9bc31f4ebc9c6b171d7bfbaa5d006ae7abdb4310 # v5.0.1

      # kubeconform publishes no container image, only release tarballs.
      - name: Install kubeconform
        run: |
          curl -fsSL -o kubeconform.tar.gz \
            https://github.com/yannh/kubeconform/releases/download/v0.8.0/kubeconform-linux-amd64.tar.gz
          echo "9bc2bffbf71f261128533edaf912153948b7ff238f9a531ae6d34466ec287883  kubeconform.tar.gz" | sha256sum -c -
          tar -xzf kubeconform.tar.gz kubeconform
          rm kubeconform.tar.gz

      - name: Lint, render and validate the chart
        run: |
          helm lint charts/otto --strict -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci
          helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci \
            | ./kubeconform -strict -summary \
                -schema-location default \
                -schema-location 'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/datreeio/CRDs-catalog/main/{{.Group}}/{{.ResourceKind}}_{{.ResourceAPIVersion}}.json'

      # The api refuses to start without a database, so the chart must refuse to
      # render one that would never come up.
      - name: Refuse to render the api without its MongoDB settings
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci \
            --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml \
            | grep -qx '                  key: url'
          for setting in api.mongoSecretName api.mongoDbName; do
            if helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
              --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci --set "$setting=" \
              --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml; then
              echo "an empty $setting must fail to render" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done

      # The retention period is a GDPR decision with no chart default, so the
      # chart must pass it through and refuse to render without one.
      - name: Render CONVERSATION_RETENTION_DAYS and refuse to render without api.conversationRetentionDays
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci \
            --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml \
            | grep -A1 -x '            - name: CONVERSATION_RETENTION_DAYS' \
            | grep -qx '              value: "30"'
          if refusal=$(helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci --set api.conversationRetentionDays= \
            --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml 2>&1); then
            echo "an empty api.conversationRetentionDays must fail to render" >&2
            exit 1
          fi; grep -q 'api.conversationRetentionDays is required' <<<"$refusal"

      # Named, the api pod runs as the account Workload Identity binds; unset,
      # the field is absent and the pod falls back to the namespace default.
      - name: Render the api pod with and without api.serviceAccountName
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci \
            --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml \
            | grep -qx '      serviceAccountName: "otto-api"'
          if helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci --set api.serviceAccountName= \
            --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml | grep -n "serviceAccountName:"; then
            echo "an empty api.serviceAccountName must render no serviceAccountName field" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      # Set, every tester is numbered from api.firstCustomerNumber and the login
      # Secret needs no customerNumbers key; unset, the pairs come from that key.
      - name: Render the api's customer numbers with and without api.firstCustomerNumber
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci \
            --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml \
            | grep -A1 -x '            - name: LOGIN_FIRST_CUSTOMER_NUMBER' \
            | grep -qx '              value: "10001"'
          if helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci \
            --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml | grep -n "key: customerNumbers"; then
            echo "api.firstCustomerNumber must leave the Secret's customerNumbers key unread" >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci --set api.firstCustomerNumber= \
            --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml \
            | grep -qx '                  key: customerNumbers'

      # The api refuses to start without TMS_MODE, and live mode without its key,
      # so the chart refuses to render either; the key only ever comes from a Secret.
      - name: Render the api's TMS mode and refuse an incomplete one
        run: |
          set -o pipefail
          helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci \
            --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml \
            | grep -A1 -x '            - name: TMS_MODE' \
            | grep -qx '              value: "stand-in"'
          helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci --set api.tmsMode=live \
            --set api.tmsBaseUrl=https://tms.example/api/ext/v1 --set api.tmsSecretName=otto-tms \
            --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml \
            | grep -A4 -x '            - name: TMS_API_KEY' \
            | grep -qx '                  key: apiKey'
          for incomplete in "api.tmsMode=" "api.tmsMode=off" "api.tmsMode=on" "api.tmsMode=live"; do
            if helm template otto charts/otto -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
              --set api.image.tag=ci --set web.image.tag=ci --set "$incomplete" \
              --show-only templates/api-deployment.yaml >/dev/null 2>&1; then
              echo "$incomplete must fail to render" >&2
              exit 1
            fi
          done

  terraform:
    # The weekly run is build-chain's alone.
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: hashicorp/setup-terraform@dfe3c3f87815947d99a8997f908cb6525fc44e9e # v4.0.1
        with:
          terraform_version: 1.16.2
          terraform_wrapper: false

      - name: Check formatting
        run: terraform fmt -check -recursive infra/terraform

      - name: Keep the compliance reader free of write and model-invoking roles
        run: |
          if grep -nE 'roles/[A-Za-z.]*(admin|editor|writer|user)"' infra/terraform/recinq-test/compliance-reader.tf; then
            echo "the compliance reader may hold no role ending in admin, editor, writer or user" >&2
            exit 1
          fi

      - name: Validate every root
        run: |
          for root in infra/terraform/modules/otto-deployer infra/terraform/modules/otto-access-identity infra/terraform/modules/otto-runtime-identity infra/terraform/recinq-test infra/terraform/access; do
            terraform -chdir="$root" init -backend=false -input=false
            terraform -chdir="$root" validate
          done

      - name: Validate audit trail routing invariants
        run: ./audit.acceptance.test.sh
        working-directory: infra/terraform/access

  images:
    # No image is built or pushed over an unacknowledged high advisory or an unpinned action (#202).
    needs: [verify, chart, build-chain]
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
      packages: write
    strategy:
      matrix:
        component: [api, web]
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: docker/setup-buildx-action@37fe631027851001ddb9b187196cc803df7f5f0e # v4.3.0

      - uses: docker/login-action@dbcb813823bdd20940b903addbd779551569679f # v4.6.0
        if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
        with:
          registry: ghcr.io
          username: ${{ github.actor }}
          password: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}

      - id: meta
        uses: docker/metadata-action@dc802804100637a589fabce1cb79ff13a1411302 # v6.2.0
        with:
          images: ghcr.io/re-cinq/otto-${{ matrix.component }}
          tags: |
            type=sha,format=long,prefix=
            type=raw,value=latest,enable={{is_default_branch}}

      # Pull requests build the image to prove the Dockerfile; only main pushes it.
      - uses: docker/build-push-action@53b7df96c91f9c12dcc8a07bcb9ccacbed38856a # v7.3.0
        with:
          context: .
          target: ${{ matrix.component }}
          push: ${{ github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main' }}
          tags: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.tags }}
          labels: ${{ steps.meta.outputs.labels }}
          cache-from: type=gha,scope=${{ matrix.component }}
          cache-to: type=gha,mode=max,scope=${{ matrix.component }}

  deploy:
    needs: images
    if: github.event_name == 'push' && github.ref == 'refs/heads/main'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    concurrency:
      group: deploy-recinq-test
      cancel-in-progress: false
    permissions:
      contents: read
      id-token: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: google-github-actions/auth@7c6bc770dae815cd3e89ee6cdf493a5fab2cc093 # v3
        with:
          workload_identity_provider: ${{ secrets.GCP_WORKLOAD_IDENTITY_PROVIDER }}
          service_account: ${{ secrets.GCP_SERVICE_ACCOUNT }}

      - uses: google-github-actions/get-gke-credentials@3da1e46a907576cefaa90c484278bb5b259dd395 # v3.0.0
        with:
          cluster_name: ${{ vars.GKE_CLUSTER_NAME }}
          location: europe-west1
          project_id: ${{ vars.GCP_PROJECT_ID }}

      - uses: azure/setup-helm@9bc31f4ebc9c6b171d7bfbaa5d006ae7abdb4310 # v5.0.1

      # Every release sends the full values, never --reuse-values: reused values
      # skip new chart defaults (Lore's nil-pointer outage). No --wait, which
      # wedges on Autopilot; the rollout step below gates instead. The deployer
      # administers only the otto namespace, which infra/terraform/recinq-test creates.
      - name: Release to the re:cinq test environment
        run: |
          helm upgrade --install otto charts/otto \
            --namespace otto \
            -f deploy/recinq-test.values.yaml \
            --set api.image.tag="${GITHUB_SHA}" \
            --set web.image.tag="${GITHUB_SHA}" \
            --cleanup-on-fail

      - name: Wait for the rollout
        run: |
          kubectl -n otto rollout status deployment/otto-api --timeout=5m
          kubectl -n otto rollout status deployment/otto-web --timeout=5m

      # The first release waits on external-dns and a Let's Encrypt certificate.
      - name: Check the public health endpoint
        run: curl -fsS --retry 20 --retry-delay 15 --retry-all-errors https://otto.gcp.re-cinq.com/api/health

      - name: Dump diagnostics
        if: failure()
        run: |
          kubectl -n otto get pods,ingress,externalsecret -o wide || true
          kubectl -n otto describe pods || true
          kubectl -n otto logs -l app.kubernetes.io/instance=otto --all-containers --tail=150 --prefix || true
          kubectl -n otto get events --sort-by=.lastTimestamp | tail -60 || true

  spec-links:
    # The weekly run is build-chain's alone.
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      # The check maps each cited file's diff since the merge base with origin/main, so it needs full history.
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      # A drifted #Lnn link fails here; `npx re-lint-reanchor` rewrites it.
      - name: Check spec line anchors
        run: npx re-lint-reanchor --check

  format:
    # The weekly run is build-chain's alone.
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@49933ea5288caeca8642d1e84afbd3f7d6820020 # v4
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      - name: Check formatting
        run: npm run prettier:check

  # #33: registerTools.ts is the one registration site; the oversight gate itself runs on beforeToolCall (#193).
  tool-registration:
    # The weekly run is build-chain's alone.
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@df4cb1c069e1874edd31b4311f1884172cec0e10 # v6
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  # Manual runs: re-checking a branch against a moved main, or confirming a gate after
  # changing one, without pushing an empty commit.
  workflow_dispatch:
  # An advisory published after a merge is invisible until someone opens a pull request, and this
  # repository can go days without one. Monday 07:00 UTC; only `build-chain` answers it.
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 7 * * 1'

# Every job here only reads the checkout; the repo default is write.
permissions:
  contents: read

# A newer push to the same branch supersedes an in-flight run. main is exempt:
# every commit there should have its own recorded result.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify
    # The scheduled run exists for the dependency audit; re-running the suite on an unchanged
    # tree every Monday would report nothing new.
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Full history, not for this job but for the spec anchor check below:
          # it resolves cited content from
          # origin/main, which a shallow clone cannot serve.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm

      # --ignore-scripts so `prepare` does not build on install: what a lifecycle script
      # runs is out of this workflow's control, and the Build step below is where a broken
      # compile should be reported. Type check catches it earlier still.
      - name: Install
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      # Every `npm run` step below is one link of the `verify` script in
      # package.json, in the same order - scripts/verify-script.test.ts holds
      # the two together - and kept as separate steps so a red run names the
      # gate that failed rather than a single opaque command.
      - name: Type check
        run: npm run typecheck

      # example/ is outside tsconfig.json's rootDir, so nothing checked the one
      # file the README and the guide are written against.
      - name: Type check the example
        run: npm run typecheck:example

      - name: Lint (--max-warnings 0)
        run: npm run eslint

      # Reports, never blocks. The one rule it runs is `warn`, so the step exits
      # 0 on its own and carries no continue-on-error: a non-zero exit here now
      # means the config itself broke, and that should fail. Its findings render
      # as warning annotations rather than failures, which is what a report on a
      # passing check should look like.
      #
      # require-statement-links counts spec statements with no test behind them.
      # Most of what it reports needs a test written rather than a line changed,
      # so the count is meant to be visible on every run and to fall over time.
      # Its test-side mirror, require-spec-link, is satisfied and gates in the
      # Lint step above. Never add a rule here to escape a red gate -
      # eslint.config.backlog.mjs says what belongs.
      - name: Spec traceability backlog (report)
        run: npm run lint:backlog

      - name: Format check
        run: npm run prettier:check

      # Runs the whole suite and fails it on the committed coverage floor in
      # jest.config.js, so this is the test gate rather than an extra pass.
      - name: Test (with coverage floor)
        run: npm run test:coverage

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      # Anchors drift silently: a cited file gaining or losing lines above the
      # cited one leaves the link pointing at different content, and the spec
      # still reads as cited. Resolves content at origin/main, which the
      # fetch-depth: 0 above exists to provide. A red check is fixed by running
      # `node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs` and committing the result.
      - name: Spec anchor check
        run: node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs --check origin/main

      # A citation counts as coverage only in its statement's trailing
      # parenthetical; one written mid-statement is dropped by the Lore job in silence,
      # so the spec reads as cited while its coverage is zero. A red check is
      # fixed by moving the link to the end of its statement, never by deleting
      # it (AGENTS.md § Spec Test Links).
      # Every fenced typescript block in the three documented files is generated
      # from source; hand transcription is what produced the defects this catches.
      - name: Documented code blocks
        run: npm run docs:check

      # Three rules that held only because somebody remembered them: a path in prose that resolves,
      # a spike that says it is a spike, and an example region inside the EU.
      - name: Documented paths resolve
        run: npm run docs:check-paths

      - name: Spike documents carry a status block
        run: npm run docs:check-spikes

      - name: Documented regions
        run: npm run check:regions

      # A line number is a derived pointer; the name is what the author cited. This catches a citation
      # whose line moved under it, which no baseline comparison can see on a branch that edits the spec.
      - name: Spec citations name their test
        run: npm run spec:names

      - name: Spec link placement
        run: npm run check:spec-links

      # Lead paragraphs and a spec's status-vs-coverage are ESLint's job; the
      # one verdict a `files` glob cannot express - that an ADR's frontmatter
      # status parses, without holding the ADR to the coverage tier - is this
      # script's. `check:spec-status -- --coverage` lists unlinked statements
      # and never gates.
      - name: Spec status
        run: npm run check:spec-status

      # A release note and a commit subject have different readers, so this is a
      # file the author writes rather than something derived from the log. The
      # label is the escape hatch for a src/ change nothing installable observes.
      - name: Changelog entry
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && !contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'no-changelog')
        # No fetch: the checkout above resolves every head into refs/remotes
        # with fetch-depth 0, and its credential is gone by the time a step
        # runs, so fetching here asked an unauthenticated git for a private
        # repository and exited 128 before the gate was ever reached.
        run: bash scripts/check-changelog.sh "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}"

  # Separate job, not a step on `verify`: these two check what the build chain
  # pulls in rather than what the code does, and a red audit should not read as
  # a failing test suite. It needs the tree installed but nothing built, so it
  # skips `prepare` with --ignore-scripts.
  build-chain:
    name: Build chain
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install (no build)
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      # Full tree, dev included: those packages are what a runner installs
      # before building dist/, and the release workflow signs what it produces.
      - name: Audit (high and above)
        run: npm run check:audit

      # A tag is a mutable pointer its owner can repoint under a job that holds
      # repository credentials.
      - name: Action pins
        run: npm run check:action-pins

  # devDependencies pins driver 7, so every other job tests 7 alone; this one
  # keeps 6, the other half of the peer range, tested.
  mongo-driver-6:
    name: Mongo driver 6
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install (no build)
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      - name: Swap in driver 6
        run: npm install --no-save --ignore-scripts mongodb@6

      - name: Type check
        run: npm run typecheck

      # --ignore-scripts skipped mongodb-memory-server's postinstall, so the first suite to start would download mongod,
      # and two suites starting together raced for one file. Fetched once here, before any worker starts.
      - name: Fetch the mongod binary once
        run: node node_modules/mongodb-memory-server/postinstall.js

      - name: Test the Mongo store
        run: npm test -- src/infrastructure/stores/mongo

  # Its own job because it is the only check that exercises the package as a
  # consumer receives it - packed, installed outside this tree, with no optional
  # peer present. Everything else here tests the source in place, where every
  # dependency is already installed and every one of these failures is invisible.
  smoke:
    name: Smoke (packed tarball)
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install (no build)
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      # Explicit, rather than relying on `npm pack` to trigger `prepare`: a build failure should be
      # reported by a step named Build, not as a confusing pack error inside the smoke script.
      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      # Two variants, two jobs' worth of signal in one: `bare` is a mock-provider consumer with no
      # optional peer, `full` is a Bedrock or Vertex consumer with both. They fail differently and
      # separate steps name which consumer is broken.
      - name: Smoke (no optional peer)
        run: npm run smoke -- bare

      - name: Smoke (both optional peers)
        run: npm run smoke -- full

### Added

- **Bound and redact what a stored conversation keeps.** `orchestrator.entries` takes two optional settings. `maxContentEntries: n` empties every entry older than the newest `n` when a turn ends; a cleared entry keeps its index, role and timestamp and is marked `cleared: true`, so no index a client holds shifts. `redactEntry(entry)` rewrites every entry but a user's once its content is final: tool calls and entries tools return before they are stored, answers and thoughts when they are committed. name: CI

on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  # Manual runs: re-checking a branch against a moved main, or confirming a gate after
  # changing one, without pushing an empty commit.
  workflow_dispatch:
  # An advisory published after a merge is invisible until someone opens a pull request, and this
  # repository can go days without one. Monday 07:00 UTC; only `build-chain` answers it.
  schedule:
    - cron: '0 7 * * 1'

# Every job here only reads the checkout; the repo default is write.
permissions:
  contents: read

# A newer push to the same branch supersedes an in-flight run. main is exempt:
# every commit there should have its own recorded result.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.ref != 'refs/heads/main' }}

jobs:
  verify:
    name: Verify
    # The scheduled run exists for the dependency audit; re-running the suite on an unchanged
    # tree every Monday would report nothing new.
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false
          # Full history, not for this job but for the spec anchor check below:
          # it resolves cited content from
          # origin/main, which a shallow clone cannot serve.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm

      # --ignore-scripts so `prepare` does not build on install: what a lifecycle script
      # runs is out of this workflow's control, and the Build step below is where a broken
      # compile should be reported. Type check catches it earlier still.
      - name: Install
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      # Every `npm run` step below is one link of the `verify` script in
      # package.json, in the same order - scripts/verify-script.test.ts holds
      # the two together - and kept as separate steps so a red run names the
      # gate that failed rather than a single opaque command.
      - name: Type check
        run: npm run typecheck

      # example/ is outside tsconfig.json's rootDir, so nothing checked the one
      # file the README and the guide are written against.
      - name: Type check the example
        run: npm run typecheck:example

      - name: Lint (--max-warnings 0)
        run: npm run eslint

      # Reports, never blocks. The one rule it runs is `warn`, so the step exits
      # 0 on its own and carries no continue-on-error: a non-zero exit here now
      # means the config itself broke, and that should fail. Its findings render
      # as warning annotations rather than failures, which is what a report on a
      # passing check should look like.
      #
      # require-statement-links counts spec statements with no test behind them.
      # Most of what it reports needs a test written rather than a line changed,
      # so the count is meant to be visible on every run and to fall over time.
      # Its test-side mirror, require-spec-link, is satisfied and gates in the
      # Lint step above. Never add a rule here to escape a red gate -
      # eslint.config.backlog.mjs says what belongs.
      - name: Spec traceability backlog (report)
        run: npm run lint:backlog

      - name: Format check
        run: npm run prettier:check

      # Runs the whole suite and fails it on the committed coverage floor in
      # jest.config.js, so this is the test gate rather than an extra pass.
      - name: Test (with coverage floor)
        run: npm run test:coverage

      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      # Anchors drift silently: a cited file gaining or losing lines above the
      # cited one leaves the link pointing at different content, and the spec
      # still reads as cited. Resolves content at origin/main, which the
      # fetch-depth: 0 above exists to provide. A red check is fixed by running
      # `node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs` and committing the result.
      - name: Spec anchor check
        run: node scripts/repoint-spec-anchors.mjs --check origin/main

      # A citation counts as coverage only in its statement's trailing
      # parenthetical; one written mid-statement is dropped by the Lore job in silence,
      # so the spec reads as cited while its coverage is zero. A red check is
      # fixed by moving the link to the end of its statement, never by deleting
      # it (AGENTS.md § Spec Test Links).
      # Every fenced typescript block in the three documented files is generated
      # from source; hand transcription is what produced the defects this catches.
      - name: Documented code blocks
        run: npm run docs:check

      # Three rules that held only because somebody remembered them: a path in prose that resolves,
      # a spike that says it is a spike, and an example region inside the EU.
      - name: Documented paths resolve
        run: npm run docs:check-paths

      - name: Spike documents carry a status block
        run: npm run docs:check-spikes

      - name: Documented regions
        run: npm run check:regions

      # A line number is a derived pointer; the name is what the author cited. This catches a citation
      # whose line moved under it, which no baseline comparison can see on a branch that edits the spec.
      - name: Spec citations name their test
        run: npm run spec:names

      - name: Spec link placement
        run: npm run check:spec-links

      # Lead paragraphs and a spec's status-vs-coverage are ESLint's job; the
      # one verdict a `files` glob cannot express - that an ADR's frontmatter
      # status parses, without holding the ADR to the coverage tier - is this
      # script's. `check:spec-status -- --coverage` lists unlinked statements
      # and never gates.
      - name: Spec status
        run: npm run check:spec-status

      # A release note and a commit subject have different readers, so this is a
      # file the author writes rather than something derived from the log. The
      # label is the escape hatch for a src/ change nothing installable observes.
      - name: Changelog entry
        if: github.event_name == 'pull_request' && !contains(github.event.pull_request.labels.*.name, 'no-changelog')
        # No fetch: the checkout above resolves every head into refs/remotes
        # with fetch-depth 0, and its credential is gone by the time a step
        # runs, so fetching here asked an unauthenticated git for a private
        # repository and exited 128 before the gate was ever reached.
        run: bash scripts/check-changelog.sh "origin/${{ github.base_ref }}"

  # Separate job, not a step on `verify`: these two check what the build chain
  # pulls in rather than what the code does, and a red audit should not read as
  # a failing test suite. It needs the tree installed but nothing built, so it
  # skips `prepare` with --ignore-scripts.
  build-chain:
    name: Build chain
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install (no build)
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      # Full tree, dev included: those packages are what a runner installs
      # before building dist/, and the release workflow signs what it produces.
      - name: Audit (high and above)
        run: npm run check:audit

      # A tag is a mutable pointer its owner can repoint under a job that holds
      # repository credentials.
      - name: Action pins
        run: npm run check:action-pins

  # devDependencies pins driver 7, so every other job tests 7 alone; this one
  # keeps 6, the other half of the peer range, tested.
  mongo-driver-6:
    name: Mongo driver 6
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install (no build)
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      - name: Swap in driver 6
        run: npm install --no-save --ignore-scripts mongodb@6

      - name: Type check
        run: npm run typecheck

      # --ignore-scripts skipped mongodb-memory-server's postinstall, so the first suite to start would download mongod,
      # and two suites starting together raced for one file. Fetched once here, before any worker starts.
      - name: Fetch the mongod binary once
        run: node node_modules/mongodb-memory-server/postinstall.js

      - name: Test the Mongo store
        run: npm test -- src/infrastructure/stores/mongo

  # Its own job because it is the only check that exercises the package as a
  # consumer receives it - packed, installed outside this tree, with no optional
  # peer present. Everything else here tests the source in place, where every
  # dependency is already installed and every one of these failures is invisible.
  smoke:
    name: Smoke (packed tarball)
    if: github.event_name != 'schedule'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@3d3c42e5aac5ba805825da76410c181273ba90b1 # v7.0.1
        with:
          persist-credentials: false

      - uses: actions/setup-node@949feb2413d6458794dcd2491c4babbbce0c15c1 # v7.1.0
        with:
          node-version: '22'
          cache: npm

      - name: Install (no build)
        run: npm ci --ignore-scripts

      # Explicit, rather than relying on `npm pack` to trigger `prepare`: a build failure should be
      # reported by a step named Build, not as a confusing pack error inside the smoke script.
      - name: Build
        run: npm run build

      # Two variants, two jobs' worth of signal in one: `bare` is a mock-provider consumer with no
      # optional peer, `full` is a Bedrock or Vertex consumer with both. They fail differently and
      # separate steps name which consumer is broken.
      - name: Smoke (no optional peer)
        run: npm run smoke -- bare

      - name: Smoke (both optional peers)
        run: npm run smoke -- full

**Score:** 1.000

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **Bound and redact what a stored conversation keeps.** `orchestrator.entries` takes two optional settings. `maxContentEntries: n` empties every entry older than the newest `n` when a turn ends; a cleared entry keeps its index, role and timestamp and is marked `cleared: true`, so no index a client holds shifts. `redactEntry(entry)` rewrites every entry but a user's once its content is final: tool calls and entries tools return before they are stored, answers and thoughts when they are committed. A redaction that throws or changes the role stores the entry cleared and logs its role. Cleared entries are left out of what the provider is sent and replayed to a resumed client as `entry_skip`, and a client is sent a tool entry as it was stored. Unset, nothing changes. `docs/session-stores.md` now lists every category of data the engine holds, where, what bounds it and what erases it.

### Fixed

- **A turn's history no longer starts with a tool result whose call was cut away.** When `contextConfig.maxMessages` cut between a tool call and its result, the provider was sent a leading tool result with no call before it, which vendors refuse. The window now starts at the first user message of text.

---

**Score:** 1.000

## Requirements

### Functional Requirements

- **FR-001**: The ADR MUST live at `adrs/ADR-001-tms-authentication.md` in `re-cinq/Otto`, following `the-expert-ui`'s `adrs/ADR-NNN-*.md` convention. (#15)
- **FR-002**: The decision issue MUST change no source file; the resolver (FR-027 to FR-042) and the TMS client and tool contract in [support-agent-tms-tools](../support-agent-tms-tools/spec.md) (#16, #19) implement the decision. (#15)
- **FR-003**: The ADR MUST record Options A and B as rejected, with a reason each (no TMS login exists for A; no per-user credential exists to hold for B). (#15)
- **FR-004**: The ADR MUST quote `KU-06`'s answer from DOA. (#15)
- **FR-005**: The ADR MUST state the token type, how a portal user obtains one, its lifetime, its refresh path, and whether the TMS scopes responses to the caller server-side. (#15)
- **FR-006**: Any of the five facts in FR-005 still unanswered MUST be listed in the ADR as an open condition naming the person who owes it, not guessed. (#15)
- **FR-007**: The ADR MUST state whether the boundary the TMS enforces is per user or per customer company, with DOA's answer as evidence. (#15)
- **FR-008**: If the boundary is per company, the ADR MUST state what stops one customer's user from reading another user's bookings inside the same company, or record that nothing does. (#15)
- **FR-009**: The ADR MUST carry a `holds_when` block listing the facts it depends on, each a checkable statement bound to the repo or party that supplies it, for example "the TMS rejects a request for a booking outside the caller's scope (`DOA`)". (#15)
- **FR-010**: The ADR MUST state, as a rule under all three options, that the customer or company id used in a TMS call is derived server-side from the authenticated identity and is never a value the model chose. (#15)
- **FR-011**: The ADR MUST decide where the `customerNumber` lives, either adopting CFOAgent's precedent (the Clerk org's `privateMetadata`, encrypted with `encryptField`) or naming the alternative. (#15)
- **FR-012**: The ADR MUST decide who writes the `customerNumber` mapping and how a wrong mapping is detected. (#15)
- **FR-013**: The ADR MUST decide the refusal for a user with no active organisation, applied on both the HTTP route and the WebSocket upgrade, in Danish (CFOAgent answers `400`). (#15)
- **FR-014**: The ADR MUST decide whether the user's role within the customer company narrows access further, given the client described customer-created users with different roles. (#15)
- **FR-015**: The ADR MUST state that per-user credential storage (Uniconta's model) is not reused, because the OLT TMS has no per-user credential to store. (#15)
- **FR-016**: The ADR MUST answer the mid-conversation token expiry question with a named behaviour: refresh, re-authenticate, or end the conversation with a Danish message. (#15)
- **FR-017**: The ADR MUST state whether `authHeaders.cookie` and `authHeaders.host` are forwarded to the TMS or stripped before the tool client sends anything, and name the issue that implements the stripping. (#15)
- **FR-018**: The ADR MUST record, for the rejected Option B, the credential store, the encryption algorithm, the key location and the cache TTL it would have used, measured against CFOAgent's shipped pattern rather than its architecture diagram, so the rejection is checkable. (#15)
- **FR-019**: When citing CFOAgent's credential pattern, the ADR MUST cite the code (Clerk `privateMetadata`) rather than the docs (Secret Manager and Firestore), and say that the two disagree. (#15)
- **FR-020**: Under Option C, the ADR MUST name the single code path where filtering happens and state that a tool bypassing it is a breach, not a bug. (#15)
- **FR-021**: The ADR MUST list the test that proves customer B's booking id returns an authorization error rather than data. (#15)
- **FR-022**: Every TMS field name the decision depends on MUST be verified against a live key, and any field still unverified MUST be recorded as an open condition rather than a guess. (#15)
- **FR-023**: The written question list sent to DOA MUST be recorded in or linked from the ADR, dated, with the re:cinq sender named. (#15)
- **FR-024**: `KU-06` MUST be updated with the date the question list was sent. (#15)
- **FR-025**: The ADR MUST name the issues that implement it: #18 (FR-027 to FR-042 here) and #16 and #19 in [support-agent-tms-tools](../support-agent-tms-tools/spec.md), each of which states in its own scope that the ADR is its input. (#15)
- **FR-026**: The ADR MUST name the `VITE_HAL_DEV_TOKEN` placeholder from [support-agent-chat](../support-agent-chat/spec.md) (#14) as what the decision replaces, together with the issue that removes it. (#15)
- **FR-027**: `apps/api/src/tools/toolAuth.ts` MUST export `TmsScopeResolver` as `(context?: ToolContext) => Promise<TmsCallScope | null>`, where `null` is a refusal no TMS request may follow (FR-030, FR-038). (#18) ([validated by `returns null for a context with no authHeaders`](../../apps/api/test/toolAuth.test.ts#L52), [validated by `returns the customer_not_verified refusal and makes no TMS call when the resolver refuses`](../../apps/api/test/defineTmsTool.test.ts#L228)).
- **FR-028**: `TmsCallScope` MUST carry `customerNumber` and no other field. (#18) ([validated by `returns customer 10001 for olt's token on the connection`](../../apps/api/test/toolAuth.test.ts#L46)).
- **FR-029**: `toolAuth.ts` MUST export `createCustomerScopeResolver(verify)`, whose resolver returns the `customerNumber` of the customer company named by the connection's verified identity, read from where ADR-001 places it (FR-011). (#18) ([validated by `returns customer 10001 for olt's token on the connection`](../../apps/api/test/toolAuth.test.ts#L46), [validated by `asks the TMS about carl's customer 20002 when the model's input names customer 10001`](../../apps/api/test/toolAuth.test.ts#L64), [validated by `resolves customer 10001 inside a tool from olt's token over a real socket, with the authorization header alone`](../../apps/api/test/toolHeaders.test.ts#L26)).
- **FR-030**: An authenticated organisation with no `customerNumber` mapped MUST produce a refusal, not an unscoped call, and MUST NOT cause a TMS request. (#18) ([validated by `refuses without a TMS call when the connection carries the token of dina, who acts for no customer company`](../../apps/api/test/toolAuth.test.ts#L87), [validated by `returns null for dina, whose token names no customer company`](../../apps/api/test/customerIdentity.test.ts#L47)).
- **FR-031**: Every tool MUST be registered through `apps/api/src/tools/registerTools.ts`, so the resolver cannot be bypassed. (#18) ([validated by `registers look_up_booking and cancel_booking behind the crash guard, each handed the input object the call carried`](../../apps/api/test/registerTools.test.ts#L37), [validated by `finds authHeaders in no tools module but toolAuth.ts`](../../apps/api/test/customerBoundary.test.ts#L21)).
- **FR-032**: `authHeaders.cookie` and `authHeaders.host` MUST NOT reach the TMS, tested with a `ToolContext` whose `cookie` and `host` are set, asserting neither string appears anywhere in the outgoing request. Whether the `authorization` value may reach the TMS is open (RD-1). (#18) ([validated by `hands the TMS call session-1 and user-42 but neither the cookie nor the host the connection carried`](../../apps/api/test/defineTmsTool.test.ts#L148)).
- **FR-033**: A tool executed with a model-supplied customer id in its input MUST reach the TMS with the resolver's scope, tested by passing a different id and asserting only the resolver's value appears in the transport request. (#18) ([validated by `passes the resolver's customer 10001 to the TMS call when the model's input names customer 20002`](../../apps/api/test/defineTmsTool.test.ts#L136), [validated by `asks the TMS about carl's customer 20002 when the model's input names customer 10001`](../../apps/api/test/toolAuth.test.ts#L64)).
- **FR-034**: Tool definitions registered in `apps/api` MUST NOT declare a customer id, company id or account number in their `inputSchema`, at any depth and in English or Danish spellings: `registerTools` MUST refuse such a definition before the registry holds it, and a test MUST walk the api's registered definitions for one. (#18) ([validated by `refuses a tool whose inputSchema declares %s`](../../apps/api/test/customerBoundary.test.ts#L31), [validated by `refuses orderer_customer_number declared inside a shipment object inside an array`](../../apps/api/test/customerBoundary.test.ts#L48), [validated by `refuses to register a tool declaring customerNumber, before the registry holds it`](../../apps/api/test/customerBoundary.test.ts#L66), [validated by `declares no customer, company or account id in any tool the api registers`](../../apps/api/test/customerBoundary.test.ts#L77)).
- **FR-035**: `auth.ws` MUST validate exactly the session the resolver later reads. (#18) ([validated by `refuses without a TMS call when the connection carries a token another issuer signed`](../../apps/api/test/toolAuth.test.ts#L75), [validated by `returns null when the Authorization header names valid-token but the offered subprotocol names other-token`](../../apps/api/test/auth.test.ts#L30)).
- **FR-036**: `auth.ws` MUST carry the authenticated customer company's id in `workspaceId`. (#18) ([validated by `returns user olt with customer 10001 as its workspaceId when the offered token verifies`](../../apps/api/test/auth.test.ts#L21)).
- **FR-037**: A connection offering an `authorization` header and a subprotocol token that differ MUST be refused: from HAL Engine 0.7.0 the engine answers it `400` before `auth.ws` runs (re-cinq/HALEngine#70), and `auth.ws` still resolves no user for it, which would answer `401` if the engine ever let one through. (#18) ([validated by `answers 400 to a real upgrade offering a valid token beside hal.v1 under an Authorization header naming forged-token`](../../apps/api/test/halSubprotocol.test.ts#L112), [validated by `returns null when the Authorization header names valid-token but the offered subprotocol names other-token`](../../apps/api/test/auth.test.ts#L30), [validated by `returns $token for headers $headers`](../../apps/api/test/bearerToken.test.ts#L5)).
- **FR-038**: A `ToolContext` with no `authorization` MUST produce a tool-result string, not a throw, and the run MUST complete with a `stream_end`. ## What is never written

- **GDPR data minimisation, Art. 5(1)(c).** No persisted document holds an `authHeaders`, `authorization`, `cookie` or `host` key at any depth, asserted by walking every key of the serialised document rather than checking its top-level fields — depth is the point rather than a flourish, since `ToolEntry.toolInput` is model-supplied data and a token can arrive nested inside a tool's input, so stripping only the top level would be theatre ([validated by: holds no credential key at any depth of the stored document](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoRedaction.test.ts#L50)).
- The redaction removes credentials and nothing else, so the guarantee is not met by writing an empty document ([validated by: keeps everything that is not a credential, so the redaction is not simply emptying the document](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoRedaction.test.ts#L57)).
- Sanitising copies rather than mutates, because the live session keeps the credentials the orchestrator hands to tools through `ToolContext` ([validated by: leaves the caller their in-memory credentials, which the tools still need](../../src/infrastructure/stores/mongo/mongoRedaction.test.ts#L82); a conversation reloaded in a fresh process therefore has no `authHeaders`, and a tool that reads them sees nothing until the caller re-authenticates, which is the intended trade-off and matches what the transport already does on socket close).

## [Unreleased]

### Added

- **Bound and redact what a stored conversation keeps.** `orchestrator.entries` takes two optional settings. `maxContentEntries: n` empties every entry older than the newest `n` when a turn ends; a cleared entry keeps its index, role and timestamp and is marked `cleared: true`, so no index a client holds shifts. `redactEntry(entry)` rewrites every entry but a user's once its content is final: tool calls and entries tools return before they are stored, answers and thoughts when they are committed. A redaction that throws or changes the role stores the entry cleared and logs its role. Cleared entries are left out of what the provider is sent and replayed to a resumed client as `entry_skip`, and a client is sent a tool entry as it was stored. Unset, nothing changes. `docs/session-stores.md` now lists every category of data the engine holds, where, what bounds it and what erases it.

### Fixed

- **A turn's history no longer starts with a tool result whose call was cut away.** When `contextConfig.maxMessages` cut between a tool call and its result, the provider was sent a leading tool result with no call before it, which vendors refuse. The window now starts at the first user message of text.
